fetchedPapers.title: Auditable and Deployable Multi-Agent Motion Planning via Posetal Games from Legal Guidelines
fetchedPapers.abstract: When robots are deployed in the real-world, they must interact with other agents and accomplish their own goals while adhering to legal constraints. These potentially conflicting objectives are often only partially prioritized, making scalarized objectives or fully specified hierarchies unsuitable. We present a framework for multi-agent motion planning under legal requirements based on games with partially ordered preferences (posetal games). Scenario-independent legal guidelines order abstract legal concerns, from which we automatically derive agent preferences and a legal game for any concrete scenario. Agents may refine their legal preferences with private objectives, and regulators may refine the guideline as laws evolve. We prove that such customizations can only remove equilibria and thus preserve legality. To coordinate agents without explicitly communicating private preferences, we introduce belief play, which provably recovers the true equilibria from conservative local games, and a distributed iterative best-response protocol requiring less information. We apply the framework to maritime navigation, systematically lifting pairwise traffic rules to multi-vessel encounters. On seven encounters with up to four vessels, every rule violation of the committed equilibria is certified as forced by the legal hierarchy or unsatisfiable, and defectors are identified from public information in all tested cases. These results indicate that guideline-based posetal games offer an auditable route from partially specified laws to multi-agent motion planning.

fetchedPapers.title: Decentralized LLM Workflows via Sequential Auctions
fetchedPapers.abstract: We present a scalable framework for solving multi-step tasks through a decentralized market of self-interested agents. Prior theoretical work demonstrated that agents organized through sequential auctions can converge to a globally optimal policy in a Markov decision process (MDP), but relied on the restrictive assumption of the existence of perfect clones as a model of perfect competition. In reality, exact clones drive agent profit to zero, violating the natural risk-reward incentives of participants. Conversely, we empirically demonstrate that the opposite extreme, absence of competition, also leads to market failure and value extraction collapse. Between these two extremes, we investigate how heterogeneous agents can survive in markets that span the critical middle ground of imperfect competition. To be profitable, agents learn to strategically shade bids to secure positive individual profit margins, while still ensuring that the marketplace functions effectively enough so that collaborative tasks posed by market consumers can still be solved. We formulate and evaluate four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, and PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, and Credit-Conserving Vickrey). Across a diverse set of domains, we demonstrate that imperfect competition successfully sustains necessary agent profit margins while maintaining high task success rates at low costs.

fetchedPapers.title: Smoothed analysis of policy iteration and value iteration for deterministic discounted and mean-payoff games played on any graph
fetchedPapers.abstract: Our understanding of turn-based stochastic games is reminiscent of our understanding of linear programming in the 1970s. Instead of the simplex method, we have two families of algorithms - policy iteration and value iteration - which work well in practice but are known to run in exponential time on some input instances, and we still lack an algorithm that runs in polynomial time on all instances. A recent result by Loff and Skomra showed that, for deterministic discounted and mean-payoff games played on an ergodic graph, a variant of policy iteration runs in smoothed polynomial time. This offered an explanation of why policy iteration performs well in practice, analogous to Spielman and Teng's explanation for the simplex method. In this paper, we drop the ergodicity assumption: we show that their policy iteration algorithms run in smoothed polynomial time for any game graph. We do this by defining a condition number that naturally generalizes theirs, showing that sufficiently-perturbed games are well-conditioned with high probability, and showing that their algorithms are efficient on well-conditioned instances. Although the outline is similar, our proof requires a substantially new approach, based on log-Lipschitz distributions which recently appeared in work on the smoothed analysis of the simplex method. For our second contribution, we propose three new value iteration algorithms for solving deterministic mean-payoff games (also on any graph). All three are based on iterative methods for finding fixed points of non-expansive operators, which we show can be applied to the Shapley operator. The first two are simple applications of Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration and Halpern iteration. The third is quadratically faster but more complicated: it runs Zwick-Paterson and Halpern iterations in parallel. We prove that all three algorithms are correct and run in smoothed polynomial time.

fetchedPapers.title: Why Alternation Speeds Up Counterfactual Regret Minimization?
fetchedPapers.abstract: Solving imperfect-information games at scale rests on counterfactual regret minimization with the regret matching$^{+}$ (RM$^{+}$) update, and a seemingly minor implementation choice accounts for much of its practical speed: alternating the two players' updates, so that the second player responds to the strategy the first player just produced. A widely repeated intuition explains why: seeing the opponent's fresh strategy should act like optimism. We treat this intuition as a testable hypothesis about deterministic two-player zero-sum self-play dynamics and find that its canonical additive form fails an information-matched test. On an analytic witness family we compare alternating RM$^{+}$ against a one-sided predictive RM$^{+}$ that receives the same information channel each round and differs only in where the fresh signal enters, a persistent regret state versus a transient prediction term. Our main result is a dichotomy theorem that reduces trajectory separation to the recurrence of exact-vertex play by the predictive dynamics: under an interior-band assumption on the alternating iterate, either vertex times recur and the profile distance is at least, infinitely often, an explicit constant that our measurements nearly attain, or they terminate. Across the tested self-play regimes, any correct explanation of the alternation speedup must reproduce a staleness cost present at the smallest tested stale fraction, an advantage that persists across seven orders of payoff conditioning, regime crossings of the optimism family, and a measured per-perturbation cost of weakening the injection path that is far steeper for staleness than for partial persistence.

fetchedPapers.title: Learning Rewards in Strategic Games
fetchedPapers.abstract: Understanding the objectives that drive agents' behavior is crucial in strategic environments, where multiple agents interact and adapt to one another. This challenge arises in domains such as cybersecurity, autonomous driving, and online markets, where agents' underlying incentives are typically unknown and must be inferred from their observed behavior. Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) provides a natural framework for this problem, but extending IRL to strategic multi-agent settings introduces a fundamental challenge: a reward that explains observed behavior does not necessarily induce optimal strategies when used for decision-making. In this work, we study this problem through the lens of \emph{strategic identifiability}, and show that learning from a fixed policy pair can be insufficient to strategically identify rewards, independent of the number of expert samples $K$. Motivated by this, we introduce an active IRL algorithm for two-player repeated Stackelberg games, in which the leader adaptively selects policies to elicit informative responses about the follower's reward. Combining maximum-likelihood estimation with experimental design, we derive finite-sample guarantees on the Stackelberg sub-optimality induced by the learned reward, matching up to polylogarithmic factors a new minimax learning rate of $K^{-1/2}$. Finally, we evaluate our approach in a realistic anti-poaching setting, demonstrating the benefits of active exploration for reward recovery and downstream strategic performance.

fetchedPapers.title: How language model agents reshape price competition
fetchedPapers.abstract: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.

fetchedPapers.title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
fetchedPapers.abstract: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems. We show how profit maximization shapes safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and several competing downstream firms. In our game-theoretic model, we derive the market-driven level of safety investment and compare it with the levels that maximize market welfare and industry profit. We find that downstream competition generally induces downstream firms to invest more in safety than the industry-profit-optimal level. By contrast, the upstream provider may underinvest relative to these benchmarks because it is not fully compensated for the surplus from safety investments. Finally, we analyze how different regulatory interventions affect the participants' incentives and profits, and the resulting levels of model safety.

fetchedPapers.abstract: The Value Problem for weighted timed games, an extension of timed automata with weights and adversity, consists in determining, given a weighted timed game with a reachability objective and a rational threshold, whether or not the value of the game exceeds the threshold. This problem is known to be undecidable for weighted timed games, i.e., there is no algorithm that can compute the value exactly. A natural alternative is to approximate the value; however, the Approximation problem is also undecidable in general. In this paper, we prove that the Approximation problem is decidable in 4-ExpTime for weighted timed games whose executions are time-bounded.

fetchedPapers.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.

fetchedPapers.title: Designing Experiments for External Decision Makers
fetchedPapers.abstract: Standard Bayesian experimental design (BED) methods assume the experimenter alone will act on the data, choosing the best action given their own beliefs and goals. In practice, data are often acted on by external parties whose procedures the experimenter cannot change and may not know, particularly when the data are released publicly. To extend BED to such settings, we introduce usage-aware experimental design, a framework in which an adaptive design policy is trained to minimise the usage risk: the experimenter's expected loss when one or more external rules act on the collected data. These rules may be non-Bayesian or black-box, and when several may apply, we either average over them or take the worst case. We show that, unlike in standard BED, more informative data can be harmful under such rules, so the usage risk cannot in general be expressed as an expected uncertainty reduction; our framework thus strictly generalises standard BED. We then use it to tackle a range of problems that are difficult to address with existing approaches.

paper.title: Auditable and Deployable Multi-Agent Motion Planning via Posetal Games from Legal Guidelines

rawOutput.titleZh: 基于法律指南的可审计与可部署多智能体运动规划通过偏序博弈

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 当机器人在真实环境中运行时，需在遵守法律约束的同时与其他智能体交互并达成自身目标。然而，法律要求往往仅部分排序，无法直接转化为传统标量代价函数。现有方法难以处理目标间的不可比性、多智能体间义务冲突及私有目标未知等问题。本文旨在构建一个能从模糊法律中自动生成可审计、可定制且可部署的多智能体决策框架。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 文章引入偏序博弈（posetal games），其中每个智能体的偏好由法律指南诱导的偏序结构定义。法律指南是一组抽象法律关切（如避碰）的优先级偏序，场景中的具体规则映射为法律度量。各智能体在此基础上加入私有目标形成最终偏好。博弈的纳什均衡即为合法行为集合，社会最优解通过公共社会指标选出。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文首次系统地将独立于场景的法律指南自动转化为多智能体博弈模型。证明了任何对偏好的细化（如添加私有目标或更新法规）只会减少而非增加合法行为集合，从而保证合法性始终被保留。在海上航行案例中，该框架成功处理了多船相遇下的规则冲突，并能审计违规行为、识别违规者。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心技术在于利用偏序偏好建模非补偿性优先级，并通过偏好细化操作保持均衡的单调性。为解决信息不完全问题，提出信念博弈协议：各智能体基于保守信念构建局部博弈，通过通信交集恢复真实均衡；另设计分布式迭代最佳响应协议，在更少信息下逼近均衡。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 框架依赖于法律度量的合理设计与动作空间的离散化，连续动作或复杂动态可能影响实用性。虽实验显示高效收敛，但最坏情况复杂度仍高。最值得读的是其将法律形式化为可计算博弈的整体架构，以及通过偏好细化保障合规性的理论洞察，为合规自主系统提供了新范式。

paper.title: How language model agents reshape price competition

rawOutput.titleZh: 语言模型代理如何重塑价格竞争

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 标准学习算法在重复伯川德竞争中通常收敛到边际成本定价的纳什均衡，消费者福利较高。然而，当大语言模型（LLM）作为定价代理时，这一结论可能被打破。本文探究LLM代理在何种条件下能维持超竞争价格，以及部署方式如何影响市场结果。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究比较了不同类型的定价代理：标准在线学习算法（如Exp3、UCB）、强化学习算法（如PPO）和基于LLM的代理。LLM代理通过提示工程、记忆机制和历史表示进行配置，形成不同的部署接口（如P-R-1、D-S-25）。市场设定为同质商品的重复伯川德竞争，企业同时定价并观察市场价格反馈。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 研究发现，LLM代理的表现高度依赖于其部署方式。P-R-1代理（逐期输出点价格，使用原始历史）能在自博弈中维持高价；而D-S-25代理（分块输出价格分布，使用汇总历史）则趋向于竞争性定价。混合部署下会出现动态模式，如‘锚定与收割’，即一个代理设定高价格锚点，另一个周期性地低价收割需求。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者采用大规模仿真实验，评估不同代理组合下的长期价格轨迹。通过分析LLM输出的决策痕迹（如plans_and_insights），识别其行为模式。构建了一个名为DBBS（向下偏置信念搜索）的代理模型，用于解释D-S-25的行为机制，并通过教师强制和自由运行测试其预测能力。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 研究局限于特定市场结构和LLM部署方式，现实中的库存、多产品等因素未被考虑。尽管如此，该论文揭示了LLM代理的定价行为对部署细节的高度敏感性，挑战了传统学习算法必然导向竞争性结果的观点。对于关注算法共谋、LLM代理设计和市场监管的研究者而言，具有重要阅读价值。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 传统Hopfield网络在从含噪样本学习原型时受限于模式间干扰（负载α）和样本熵p，导致泛化能力下降。本文探究当使用指数型Hopfield网络作为注意力层时，能否摆脱负载限制，在不提供标签的情况下从模糊样例中恢复原始原型，并揭示其泛化与记忆之间的相变行为。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型将训练样本直接作为键值对存入指数Hopfield网络，查询为新的同类噪声样本。通过调节softmax温度β，观察单步更新后输出与真实原型的重叠度m(1)及与最近训练样本的相似度nmax。使用合成Rademacher数据与二值化MNIST/Fashion-MNIST进行验证。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 发现存在一个随规模√N扩展的泛化窗口：在此区间内，模式间干扰呈指数级衰减，允许学习指数级数量的原型；超出则进入记忆态。该过程对应随机能量模型的冻结相变，且在真实数据上可检测子簇结构，最优性能出现在记忆阈值之后而非之前。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 采用信号-噪声比分析法，推导出注意力熵peff替代传统数据熵p，统一描述加权投票的噪声水平。证明在中间β区，交叉干扰项指数衰减使负载失效；高β下softmax权重集中于单一样本，形成记忆。REM框架解释了权重分布与相变位置。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 理论基于高斯近似，在高度凝聚态下会高估磁化强度；假设样本独立同分布，难以完全刻画真实数据复杂结构。最值得阅读的是其将注意力动态映射为物理相变的视角，以及记忆非失败而是有用操作的新认知。

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么多任务优化在多目标场景下缺乏理论支持？尽管进化多任务优化（EMTO）在实践中展现出跨任务知识迁移的优势，但其效率提升始终缺乏严格的数学证明，尤其是在多目标优化领域。现有理论仅限于单目标问题，而多目标情况因涉及非支配排序和拥挤距离等复杂机制，使得运行时间分析极具挑战。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文研究了MO-MFEA算法在同时求解两个相似双目标问题时的表现。输入是两类二进制空间上的最大化问题，输出是覆盖各自帕累托前沿的解集。通过定义结构相似的任务对（如OMM/OJZJ、LOTZ/DLTB），分析算法在不同任务间传递知识的能力，并以期望函数评估次数作为核心性能指标。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文首次为多任务多目标优化提供了数学运行时间证据。结果显示，在合理参数下，MO-MFEA能在O(n²logn)时间内同时解决简单任务OMM和复杂任务OJZJ，相比单独优化OJZJ实现了O(n⁻¹/logn)的速度提升，且总耗时不高于单独优化简单任务。这证明知识迁移确实可加速难任务求解。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者采用概率分析与种群动态建模相结合的方法，刻画跨任务个体配对与交叉的概率。关键在于利用标量适应度排序维持各任务资源平衡，并通过引理量化优秀解被选中参与繁殖的可能性。结合非支配排序与拥挤距离机制，建立了从种群状态到收敛时间的完整推导链条。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 结论依赖于特定构造的结构相似任务对，现实问题的相似性更难界定。此外，分析聚焦渐近阶数，未考虑常数因子或实际计算开销。最值得阅读的是其理论框架本身——如何将复杂的多任务进化过程转化为可分析的数学模型，这对后续EMTO理论研究具有奠基意义。

rawOutput.titleZh: 超越汉明悬崖：保持语义距离的紧凑空间编码在脉冲神经网络中的应用

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 脉冲神经网络（SNN）采用空间编码可避免时间积分带来的延迟，但标准二进制编码存在‘汉明悬崖’问题——相邻数值的编码汉明距离极大，破坏语义邻近性。这导致监督STDP学习中因权重抵消需大幅增益，引发误报。现有编码如格雷码虽消除悬崖却无法保持全局语义结构，而热计码又过于冗长，难以部署于硬件。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究在SpiNNaker硬件上构建双轨输入、单输出神经元的SNN，使用STDP规则进行监督学习。输入为0-255整数范围内的所有值，分别经二进制、格雷、热计、约翰逊及四种混合编码预处理为空间模式。通过测量分类精度、假阳性率及增益容忍度，评估各编码在训练多个连续值时的表现，并扩展至1024值范围测试输入容量限制。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出一类混合编码，结合粗粒度热计/约翰逊码与细粒度格雷码，在极小宽度下保留高相关性的语义-汉明距离映射。实验证明，热计与约翰逊码能实现语义区间容忍，而混合编码以约1/8宽度达到类似效果，且在1024值下仍适配硬件输入限制，显著优于传统方案。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 混合编码将数值分为块索引与偏移量，前者用热计或约翰逊码编码以保持距离单调性，后者用反射格雷码确保跨块边界仅变一位。通过反射奇偶块内偏移方向，避免块间跳跃。该设计使网络容忍半径在语义空间形成连续区间，且其大小由增益与编码参数决定，而非依赖全宽编码。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 实验基于合成数据与单一网络结构，未涉及真实多特征任务，且权重叠加非在线顺序学习，可能影响实际收敛。结论对语义连续输入的SNN系统设计具指导意义，最值得阅读的是其对编码几何如何决定网络泛化行为的机制分析与硬件兼容性论证。
